# MachSig trust gate — review packet (step 5 of the ruling of 2026-10-13)

Generated by `tools/machsig/transition.py`; deterministic. Companion to `TRANSITION_2026-10-13.md`. **2 removals, 2 restatements, 3833 changes affecting proof assumptions** (every grew/shrank/swap whose axiom delta is not standard-Lean-only), 0 involving sorryAx, compiler trust or an undeclared axiom.

## For a reviewer who has never seen MachLib

MachLib is a Lean 4 library with **no Mathlib**: the real numbers are themselves axiomatised (`MachLib.Real : Type`, `addR`, `mul_comm`, `exp`, `exp_add`, … are `axiom` declarations). So almost every theorem rests on dozens of MachLib axioms, and a theorem's *footprint* — what `#print axioms` lists — is its whole trusted base. Lean's own three standard axioms are `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

`foundations/AxiomLedger.lean` declares the policy. `knownAxioms` is every live axiom; `trustedFootprint` is the approved foundation. The theorem ledger (`tools/theorem_ledger/ledger.py`) puts each theorem in one tier: **approved_policy** (footprint inside `trustedFootprint`), **conditional** (uses a declared axiom outside it; the record names which), **unchecked** (sorryAx, compiler trust, or an undeclared axiom).

The gate (`tools/machsig/trust_gate.py`) is a ratchet: for a theorem whose statement did not change, no axiom may enter its footprint without a reviewed rebaseline. Between 2026-09-03 and 2026-10-13 it compared stale signatures and saw nothing. This packet lists what it missed that a person must judge.

**Why so many footprints GREW without anything getting less trustworthy.** On 2026-10-04 three commits turned 39 axioms into theorems or definitions (`exp_pos`, `natCast`, `mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right`, …). A theorem that used `exp_pos` as an axiom now uses its *proof*, which rests on more basic axioms (`exp_add`, `exp_surj`, field axioms). So `exp_pos` leaves the footprint and those enter: the count grows, while the set of things assumed shrinks to the foundation. The report checks this mechanically for each change (section 4 there); section C1 below is what it does not explain.

**What to decide**, per item: is the change intended and acceptable? Concretely: (A) a removed theorem was meant to go, or moved; (B) a restated theorem's new statement is the intended one; (C) an axiom entering a footprint is one the theorem should rest on, and a conditional axiom leaving is a real discharge. Mark rejections; the baseline is committed only after every section is signed off.

**Check any line yourself** (from `foundations/` of a built tree at either revision):

```
printf 'import MachLib\n#print axioms MachLib.Real.exp_nonneg\n' > /tmp/p.lean && lake env lean /tmp/p.lean
git log --oneline 23e0d047..c3046961 -- foundations/MachLib/<File>.lean
```

Full per-theorem axiom sets for every section: `transition_2026-10-13.json` (`rows[].old.axiom_set`, `rows[].new.axiom_set` → `axiom_sets`). Sections A, B and C1 print them inline.
